title: Paragraph / section function Practice 1
description: 4 short texts - 8 focused paragraph / section function questions
subject: rla
passage:
TEXT A - Cooling Pavement

A city article first explains that dark asphalt can become extremely hot in direct sun. The next paragraph describes a reflective coating tested on two blocks. A third paragraph reports surface-temperature measurements from coated and uncoated areas.

TEXT B - Volunteer Training

A volunteer handbook explains the responsibilities of event greeters. One paragraph gives a short dialogue showing how to respond when a visitor asks for an accessible entrance.

TEXT C - Shared Bikes

A report praises a bike-share expansion for increasing access near train stations. The final paragraph notes that several outer neighborhoods still have no stations within walking distance.

TEXT D - River Sensors

An article explains how low-cost sensors collect water-level readings. The next section describes a flood in which those readings gave officials earlier warning than a manual gauge.

questions.prompt: What is the main function of this paragraph or section?
questions.explanation: The paragraph reports measurements from coated and uncoated areas, so its job is to evaluate the tested response with evidence.
questions.rule: Name the relationship first, then prove it with the surrounding text.

options.text: provides measured evidence that evaluates whether the reflective coating reduced surface temperature
introduces the problem of dark asphalt becoming extremely hot
options.whyWrong: That is the job of the opening paragraph, not the measurement paragraph named in the question.

options.text: explains how the reflective coating was applied to the test blocks
options.whyWrong: Application belongs to the pilot description; the target paragraph reports results.

options.text: recommends coating every city surface based on the pilot
options.whyWrong: Reporting a comparison does not by itself make a citywide recommendation.

questions.prompt: How does this part contribute to the larger text?
questions.explanation: The paragraph contributes evaluation: it lets readers judge the proposed response using measured outcomes.
questions.rule: Name the relationship first, then prove it with the surrounding text.

options.text: It returns to the original heat problem without adding evidence about the coating.
options.whyWrong: The target moves beyond the problem by reporting the test results.

options.text: It explains the installation procedure in greater technical detail.
options.whyWrong: The paragraph is about measured outcomes, not the coating procedure.

options.text: It moves the article from describing the pilot to evaluating it with observed results.
It shifts from the roof test to an unrelated discussion of city budgets.
options.whyWrong: Nothing in the described section signals a topic shift to budgets.

questions.prompt: What is the main function of this paragraph or section?
questions.explanation: The dialogue turns the handbook's general responsibilities into a concrete example of how the guidance works.
questions.rule: Name the relationship first, then prove it with the surrounding text.

options.text: illustrates the greeter guidance with a realistic visitor interaction
defines the general responsibilities of event greeters
options.whyWrong: The handbook already explains the responsibilities; the target dialogue shows them in use.

options.text: adds a new accessibility rule that changes the handbook policy
options.whyWrong: An example of responding to a visitor does not establish a new rule.

options.text: argues that most visitors need help finding accessible entrances
options.whyWrong: One dialogue illustrates a situation; it does not show how most visitors behave.

questions.prompt: How does this part contribute to the larger text?
questions.explanation: The dialogue makes an abstract instruction practical by demonstrating its application.
questions.rule: Name the relationship first, then prove it with the surrounding text.

options.text: It supplies survey evidence that visitors prefer one entrance over another.
options.whyWrong: A dialogue is an example, not survey evidence.

options.text: It shows how the general instructions can guide an actual response to a visitor.
It contrasts two competing accessibility policies for event sites.
options.whyWrong: The passage describes one response, not a policy comparison.

options.text: It replaces the greeter responsibilities with a different set of duties.
options.whyWrong: The example applies the existing guidance rather than replacing it.

questions.prompt: What is the main function of this paragraph or section?
questions.explanation: The final paragraph limits the earlier praise by noting neighborhoods that still lack nearby stations.
questions.rule: Name the relationship first, then prove it with the surrounding text.

options.text: adds another benefit that strengthens the claim that access improved everywhere
options.whyWrong: The missing stations are a limitation, not another benefit.

options.text: explains the technical reason bike-share stations require train connections
options.whyWrong: The paragraph identifies a geographic gap; it does not explain station technology.

options.text: recommends removing stations from the neighborhoods near train stations
options.whyWrong: The text reports an access gap, not a proposal to remove existing stations.

options.text: qualifies the positive evaluation by identifying a remaining access gap

questions.prompt: How does this part contribute to the larger text?
questions.explanation: The limitation adds balance: expansion helped near stations, but some outer neighborhoods remain underserved.
questions.rule: Name the relationship first, then prove it with the surrounding text.

options.text: It proves the expansion failed because any remaining gap cancels the earlier benefit.
options.whyWrong: A remaining limitation does not erase the access gains already described.

options.text: It prevents the report from implying that the expansion improved access equally across the city.
It changes the topic from transportation access to neighborhood population growth.
options.whyWrong: The paragraph stays focused on access to bike-share stations.

options.text: It explains how residents in outer neighborhoods travel to train stations.
options.whyWrong: The paragraph notes the absence of nearby stations but does not describe residents' travel behavior.

questions.prompt: What is the main function of this paragraph or section?
questions.explanation: The flood example shows the earlier-described sensor system mattering in an actual event.
questions.rule: Name the relationship first, then prove it with the surrounding text.

options.text: explains the technical process by which the sensors collect water-level readings
options.whyWrong: The earlier section explains collection; the flood case shows the system in use.

options.text: compares several sensor brands to determine which is most accurate
options.whyWrong: No brand comparison appears in the described case.

options.text: introduces a limitation showing that manual gauges are always more reliable
options.whyWrong: The example says the sensor readings provided earlier warning than a manual gauge.

options.text: provides a real case that demonstrates the practical value of the sensor readings

questions.prompt: How does this part contribute to the larger text?
questions.explanation: The case connects the technology to a real outcome, strengthening the explanation of why the sensors can matter.
questions.rule: Name the relationship first, then prove it with the surrounding text.

options.text: It proves low-cost sensors will predict every flood accurately.
options.whyWrong: One useful case cannot support an absolute claim about every flood.

options.text: It explains how to install sensors beside a manual gauge.
options.whyWrong: The section demonstrates usefulness rather than installation steps.

options.text: It demonstrates a concrete consequence of the technology: officials received earlier warning during a flood.
It shifts the article away from water monitoring to the cost of flood damage.
options.whyWrong: The example remains part of the article's discussion of water-level monitoring.

curriculum.learningObjective: Apply paragraph / section function reasoning across varied original texts and explain answers from textual evidence.
